# **~~BME’s COPPER B~~ RIEFING** **~~S~~ ERVICE** ## **January 2009** ##### **Copper surplus of one million tonnes over Q4 2008 - Q3 2009 looks likely** BME’s current assessment is that for the twelve months from October 2008 through September 2009, in copper there will be an excess of refined production over refined consumption of around one million tonnes. Between endDecember 2009 and end-January 2009, LME stocks of copper increased by 150 kt, or almost 45%, from around 340 kt to 490 kt. Mostly, we believe this to be a simple reflection of a huge current surplus. However, there was undoubtedly also some relocation of stock, as financing off-warrant stocks became more difficult. The relocated element of the LME stock build represents unsold producer and merchant material that began building up on a big scale as long ago as August in Zambia and September in Chile. LME cash prices fell below $3,000 per tonne in the second half of December 2008, but have recovered to a little over $3,000 per tonne in January despite the huge LME stock build that month. As the chart on the back page shows, the LME stock to LME cash price curve has turned almost horizontal now, as it does tend to do once prices have fallen into the mine cost structure. Even the very modest partial price recovery that has taken place is puzzling if one tries to interpret it simply in old-fashioned ways, i.e. according to surplus or deficit. But in the short term, today’s commodity prices are driven much more directly by other markets and by sentiment. Copper prices have been responding to the new US administration’s approach to stimulus packages, and also to the evidence that the Chinese stimulus packages are now beginning to show promise. We remain of the view that prices will fall below $3,000 per tonne and stay there for some time. At today’s prices, just above $3,000, the Chinese SRB is understood to have contracted to take small tonnages monthly directly from producers, but not on a scale sufficient to buoy the price. Their present target is said to be a 100 kt copper stock build. We think that if we are correct that prices will fall a little below $3,000 then stabilise, while exchange stocks continue to rise, then the SRB may well buy much larger tonnages on the exchanges, provided that it finds it can do so without moving the price higher. That we think will be the pattern in the second half of this year. The South Korean stockpile may also absorb some material. Custom smelters may also help stabilise the cathode market, if they cut throughput sufficiently sharply to force excess mine production to build up as concentrates stocks rather than cathode. Recent high TC/RCs suggest that they may be doing that right now, but with far more mine cuts looming, we are still far from convinced that this pattern will endure. **By Peter Hollands, February 4****th** **2009** 500 Commercial balance because

1 **© 2008: Bloomsbury Minerals Economics Ltd** **www.bloomsburyminerals.com** ### **Macroeconomic trends** As predicted in our December Copper Briefing, **the economic recession is proving deeper than originally thought** as the official data and economic forecasts based upon it come in. As a firm benchmark, CHR data shows Industrial Production falling by 2.4% year-onyear in October. It estimates a 5.2% drop in November. We are now looking at a contraction in global production of more than 4% on an annual basis in Q4 2009 and a larger (8%) fall quarter-on-quarter. This is an extremely rapid rate of contraction, and it is hardly surprising that CHR has downgraded its growth forecast for 2009. It now forecasts a 3.3% annual fall in IP. **China** , in particular, is a cause for concern. Having consistently recorded well above the official minimum target of 8% p.a. growth, in the fourth quarter of 2009 GDP was up on the previous year by only 6.8%. This reflected zero growth on the previous quarter. There is worse to come. Electricity use, a good forward indicator of industrial output, was down by 6% in the OctoberDecember quarter. There are widespread reports of factories closing and migrant workers returning from the cities to their rural homes. IP is likely to fall further as exports, surprisingly resilient to date, fall further. HSBC forecasts that Chinese exports will be down by 19% year-on-year in the first quarter of this year. Although the backcloth in China is not encouraging, with a large fiscal surplus and positive current account balance, the Chinese government can tackle the issue aggressively. The much discussed RMB 4 trillion stimulus package, targeted largely at infrastructure, has been followed by ot

her measures to prop up domestic demand. These include a 13% rebate on sales of home appliances to rural residents, cuts in interest rates, the scrapping of controls on bank lending and a large reduction in the down payment required to buy a home. Perhaps more important than any of these measures is the potential for direct intervention of government, still the owner of the banks and one-third of Chinese industry, in this formerly centrally planned economy. **Other major export orientated Asian economies** are doing much worse than China. Exports from Japan, Korea and Taiwan are each down by around 35% compared to a year ago. Not surprisingly, this drastic reduction is reflected in the IP numbers. In the fourth quarter of 2009, IP in Japan and Korea was down by around 10% compared to the previous year; Taiwan’s output was down by nearly 20%. While the situation in **Japan** is dire, however, there are reasons to believe that the country may be early out of the recession. Japan has a healthy current account surplus and minimal household debt. At present companies are busy cutting back, but the banks here are willing and able to offer credit where needed. Indeed, bank lending to companies is rising. Japan’s domestic demand may pick up quite quickly and the country should be well poised to benefit once global demand for its goods begins to rebound. Hope of an early recovery in the more spendthrift **United States** and parts of **Europe** is more distant. Credit is the most obvious problem. In the United Kingdom a second injection of cash into the banks has been announced, the first one late last year having failed to restore confidence or renew lending. The same may be overdue in the United States. Even if huge government spending by these countries, with minimal reserves to afford it, averts a banking system collapse, it is now clear that consumer behaviour will not easily return to the pattern of the past. For many years some countries, notably the US, the UK and Spain, have run up huge current account deficits, money from abroad helping to finance cheap credit and high consumer spending in relation to income, which resulted in asset over-valuation. With funding no longer available and a new mood of realism, it is likely to be a long time before the all-important consumers in these crucial markets return to fuel growth in the global economy. ##### **By Paul Dewison** Industrial production year‐on‐

**.**|**.**|**.**|**.**| ### **Consumption trends** With the more bleak economic picture emerging, **we have revised our consumption forecasts in line with the Pessimistic Case** presented in the December Briefing. We now forecast a 5.8% fall in refined consumption in 2009, followed by a 7.9% rebound in 2010. The rate of decline is slightly less than in our December (pessimistic scenario) figure not because we see 2009 turning out any better than anticipated, but because the baseline for 2008 was lower. We estimate that consumption in the fourth quarter of last year was 8.9% down on 2007. Although orders at fabricators have picked up a little, fabricators are showing **little willingness to commit to long term copper purchase contracts** . When orders for cathode do pick up, we may expect a revival in spot purchasing, raising spot premia above their current rockbottom levels (US$20-30/t in Europe). Even where orders have picked up, **consumption is still tracking downwards,** as orders were thin in the last quarter of 2008. We forecast global refined copper consumption in the first quarter of 2009 as being 11.5% lower than in 2008. Consumption should continue to be lower than last year for the second and third quarters of this year. But, in absolute terms, the January-March quarter should be the low point, as consumption should pick up sequentially from this point on. The rate of consumption right now is exceptionally low, the anticipated 4.1 Mt figure for this quarter being the lowest for five years. The current rate of LME stock build (7-8 kt per day) should be seen in this conte

xt. An announcement by the copper/alloy products mill **Swissmetal** in **Europe** illustrates the current market state. The company characterised the market situation as positive but erratic. Referring to the first three weeks of 2009, it reported order intake considerably above 2008, but said that over the past three month orders were down by 41% on the comparable period in 2007/08. Looking at specific markets, it saw orders in the power infrastructure related generator sector, already strong, getting stronger. There were also improvements in the less strong industrial goods and electronics-related connectors sector, while other OEM goods markets remained weak. Despite the improvement in orders, with continued low output volumes, the company accompanied this market assessment by announcing temporary capacity cutbacks and job cuts. The sense of uncertainty that underlies the Swissmetal statements is common to other fabricators in Europe and elsewhere. Smelters in **Japan** , for example, are reporting great difficulty in placing any material on term contract for the January to March period, term deals being signed for delivery starting in March. Clearly, for many fabricators, output is turning out to be much lower than had been planned. An early indication of what this might mean for the results of Japanese fabricators has been provided by **Hitachi Cable** . The company has revised Apportionmentof Global Copper

While lower copper prices contributed towards the lower revenue figure, smaller volumes and margins were much more important, with huge volume falls in automotive and semiconductor business. Hitachi Cable had previously expected a small Yen ¥5 billion net loss. It now expects to lose ¥53 billion, losses coming from costs associated with restructuring and extraordinary items relating to the harsh market conditions as well as direct trading losses. The state of the Japanese market is indicated in figures released by its fabricator industry associations. In November, shipments of cable were down by 16% and mill products by 19% on 2007. Substantially worse f

igures were anticipated for December. The associations estimate shipment of both products being down by 5% and 6% respectively for 2008 in total. Especially weak demand is cited in automotive and electronics sectors, with construction-based demand also performing badly. Tube demand for air conditioners is holding up comparatively well. Similarly bleak financial results for fabricators are expected in other parts of the world. The information cable firm **Belden** , operating in **North America** and Europe, was early to release downgraded estimates for 2008 based on its fourth quarter performance. Belden revised its annual revenue forecast from US$2.1 billion to US$2.0 billion, implying fourth quarter revenue of US$425 million, 15% down on 2007. Not surprisingly, earnings per share estimates for the quarter were slashed, by upwards of 70%. The company was early to address the tougher conditions by announcing a restructuring early in December that would mean losing 1,800 employees, or 20% of company staff. We may expect similar financial results and cutbacks to be announced by other fabricators in weeks to come. While the dire market state in most places is clear, data for **China** are ambiguous. Recent data show fabricated products output in 2008 up by 19%, but apparent refined consumption up by only 4.4%. Import figures are similarly inconclusive. Imports of refined copper were up by over a third on 2007 in November and December which, despite flat output, suggests that apparent consumption late in 2008 was up considerably on the previous year. This does not tally with what fabricators are saying, where demand is reported to be down in OEM sectors (especially air conditioners) and construction. Part of the explanation lies in arbitrage buying. As the price incentive to purchase on spot existed well into December, with delivery scheduled for January and February, we see an ongoing stock build in in China continuing in coming weeks. Unless some of the slack is taken up by the SRB, therefore, we see China as being a negative force in the refined copper market for some time to come as stocks are worked off. **By Paul Dewison** QuarterlyGlobal Consumption and Annual

At Escondida ore grades are now at their lowest for many years at 1.04% and falling. BHP Billiton, which owns the controlling stake in the mine, has also announced that it has suspended the Phase 5 development program at Escondida for at least 18 months. The mine may produce at a rate of only 600 ktpy of copper-in-concentrates until prices recover. Freeport McMoRan has further cut its production forecasts for 2009 and 2010. The Morenci mine in Arizona is where most of the latest cut has been. The company intends to bring operating costs across its North American mines down to below $1.25/lb copper. Copper ore grades
Seemingly the only positive mine production news has come from the Grasberg mine, where ore grades have recovered as the mining focus has moved through a phase of low grade mining into a higher grade phase. Freeport expects high grade ore mining to continue throughout 2009. It must be remembered that the increase in concentrate production from the mine is coming from a multi-year low base in mid-2007. ##### **More labour unrest** Labour unions across the globe have reacted aggressively to recent severe job cuts. In copper, Peru’s National Miners’ Union has been the first national mining union to react to the contraction of employment in the mining industry. The recent drop in metals prices has jeopardised the billions of dollars of investment money on new projects in Peru that would create 1,000’s of jobs. In conference call regarding the fourth quarter production results, Grupo Mexico sugge

In the first case of perhaps many future, small scale nationalisations, Zambian Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) has taken control of Luanshya Copper Mine’s Baluba mine. ZCCM intends to operate the mine, which was put on care and maintenance late last year, until an international buyer can be found for the property, however, it may be some time until that occurs. ##### **Production costs** Antofagasta’s latest quarterly report shows a distinct increase in production costs for its Los Pelambres mine, a reflection of the lower by-product credits for molybdenum and their effect on cash costs. Vedanta’s third quarter report, for FY 2008-2009, shows that its Konkola complex’s production remains high on the cost curve. However, it has now chosen to switch entirely to the new Nchanga smelter and away from its Nkana smelter to optimise production costs. It has also approached nearby mining operations to sign direct ore shipment deals to further optimise cash flows. ##### **Smelter Capacity Cuts** Pan Pacific Copper (PPC), Sumitomo Metal Mining, and Mitsubishi Metals Corp have joined a long list of smelters that have decided to cut output for 2009. PPC has already announced that it has cut production by 5%, and may further cut production by 20%. Mitsubishi, which owns the Gresik smelter, which takes a lot of feed from the Grasberg mine, has decided to cut production of refined copper by 10% after February this year. Sumitomo plans to cut production in the second half of FY 2009 by 7%. All these smelters are citing slowing copper demand and lower prices as the reasons for the cut. ##### **By Christopher Welch** Percentage Capacity Utilization

##### **Stocks could hit 700 kt** We have increased the forecast refined copper surplus to 915 kt for this year, from our forecast of 544 published last month, to factor in the worsening demand outlook (see consumption section). LME stock increases are likely to continue to at least 700 kt this year, and liquid stocks as a whole (exchanges, merchant and bonded stocks), may approach 1.5 Mt, up from just over 1 Mt. The SRB is reported to have contracted to buy modest monthly tonnages from producers and to have current plans to buy 100 kt. BME thinks they will buy far more than that if prices fall below $3,000 and exchange stocks pile up. ##### **LME stocks soar in January** LME stocks climbed at an average of 7 kt per working day in January, taking the total to almost 500 kt, the highest level of LME stocks since 2004. With cancelled warrants remaining below 2% of total stocks, there is little chance of a significant draw down in the near future. LME stocks have risen 150 kt since the end of 2008, but nearly all of the stock increase has come into warehouses in the USA and Europe, in particular, Rotterdam which now holds ~25% of LME copper stocks, having taken in 30 kt in January, according to Reuters data. Little stock was added to Asian LME warehouses last month, however. The three Korean warehouse destinations saw an increase of only 10 kt, or 7% of the total stock increase on the LME. The Singapore warehouses’ stock increased by only 5 kt, or 3% of the LME stock increase. The data available from Reuters showed that the warehouses at Singapore, Busan, Korea as well as Livorno, Italy, had the most withdrawals. Lower ore grades at the Cadia Hill mine, which are expected to continue for most of the the first half of 2009, negated improved recovery rates at the Ridgeway mine. The company’s **Telfer** mine in Western Australia, produced 7.2 kt of copper during the fourth quarter of 2008, up 0.7 kt from the year earlier period. The Scuddles and Gossan Hill mines are part of the **Golden Grove** operation. In other news, the company has secured a bridge financing facility of A$140 million which will cover short-term cash requirements for the operation of the company’s Golden Grove and **Martabe** mines, as well as development capital for its **Prominent Hill** copper project, which it expects to enter production during the first half of this year. _Oz Minerals press release, January 13__th_ _& January 22__nd_

**BHP Billiton** may reduce production from its **Olympic Dam** Cu-Au-U mine this year, due to lower base metals prices. _Mining Journal, January 23_<sup>_rd_</sup> _2009._ 

**Aditya Birla Minerals** has placed its **Mt Gordon** mine on care and maintenance due to lower copper prices. Processing of run of mine ore stockpiles will produce 1.8 kt of copper-in-concentrate in 2009, after which the stockpile will have been depleted. Mt Gordon produced 11 kt of copper last year. Aditya has also suspended crushing and stacking at its **Nifty** mine, but will continue the leaching operation whilst it remains economic. _Thomson Reuters, January 7_<sup>_th_</sup> _2009._ 

**Botswana: African Copper** has suspended production from its **Mowana** mine for a minimum of three weeks so that the company can focus on raising necessary capital. African Copper is currently in discussions with financers to raise additional capital to cover a cashflow shortfall created by lower than expected production from the mine in 2008. The lower than expected production was due to a delay in commissioning of the mine. In the last quarter the mine produced 0.3 kt of copper-in-concentrates, down significantly from its earlier production guidance of 1.5 kt. _Thomson Reuters, January 21_<sup>_st_</sup> _2009._ 

**Brazil: Yamana Gold** has completed a feasibility study on the phased expansion of its **Chapada** gold-copper mine. The expansion remains on schedule to enter production 

this year, but the company has advised that this is dependent on metals prices. _Thomson Reuters, January 20_<sup>_th_</sup> _2009._ 

**Canada: Xstrata** has announced that it will lose 55 permanent jobs at its **Horne** smelter due to the closure of **First Metals’ Fabie** mine, a custom milling client of the smelter. Having reassessed the economic situation of the Horne complex, Xstrata has also decided to reduce its recycled feed, and to cut planned capital expenditures. First Metals announced in December that it would close the mine, which has become uneconomic to operate at current copper prices. First Metals expected all mining activities to have ceased in January 2009. _Xstrata press release, January 15_<sup>_th_</sup> _2009._ 

Production from **Northgate Mineral’s Kemess South** mine during the fourth quarter was lower than expected due to a water pipe bursting in December, leading to a six day production loss. The mine produced 6.5 kt of copperin-concentrate, down from the expected 8.4 kt. Grades also fell in the last quarter, averaging 0.196% copper, down from 0.238% in the year earlier period, as more waste rock had to be removed from the western end of the pit following, localised sloughing earlier in 2008. Mining of the western end will be completed in the first half of this year. The mine produced 23.5 kt of copper during 2008, down from 30.9 kt in 2007. Northgate Minerals expects the mine to produce 24.5 kt of copper during 2009. _Northgate Minerals press release, January 1

**Chile: Antofagasta’s Los Pelambres** mine produced 85.4 kt of payable copper in the fourth quarter of 2008, a decrease of 5.1% compared to the preceding quarter. The decrease in production is due to a scheduled maintenance shutdown in December. The mine also produced 2.1 kt of molybdenum during the quarter, an increase of 10.5% compared to the preceding quarter due to improved molybdenum grades, which offset the lower plant throughput. Cash costs in the last quarter were $2,560/t compared to $882/t in the preceding quarter. The higher production costs were due to a significant drop in the price of molybdenum which is the by product credit at the Los Pelambres mine. Antofagasta’s **El Tesoro** mine produced 22.6 kt of cathode during the fourth quarter of 2008, up 5.1% from the preceding quarter. Cash costs at the mine were $3,166/t during the last quarter, down 6.6% from the preceding quarter, due to lower input costs. The company expects the mine to produce 95 kt of cathode this year as it begins processing higher grade ore from the North-East deposit at El Tesoro as well as commencing the heapleaching of low grade ore taken from the nearby Esperanza project. The company has reduced the stripping rate at the project by 40% to allow for the lower copper price. The **Michilla** mine produced 12.3 kt of cathode in the fourth quarter of last year, an increase of 5.8% compared to the preceding quarter. Production costs at Michilla also fell due to the lower input costs. During the last quarter cash costs were $3,809/t. _Antofagasta press release, February 3rd 2009._

**Kazakhstan: Kazakhmys** expects to reduce cathode production, from its own concentrate, by 10-15% in 2009, in response to lower copper prices and weakening global copper demand. **Laos: PanAust’s Phu Kham** mine produced 13 kt of copper-in-concentrates during the fourth quarter of 2008, its second quarter in production.

**Peru: Grupo Mexico’s** operating subsidiary, **Southern Copper Corp** , has announced that it has suspended or will evaluate all capital expenditure plans. The **Cerro Verde** mine, in which **Freeport McMoRan** holds a controlling stake, produced 148 kt of recoverable copper during the fourth quarter of 2008, up from 143 kt in the year earlier period. Domestic production totalled 116.6 kt of copper in December. This is an increase of 5.74% compared to the year earlier period, according to the Energy & Mines Ministry. Peru produced a total of 1.267 Mt in 2008. _Thomson Reuters, January 23_<sup>_rd_</sup> _2009._ 

**Philippines: OceanaGold** has suspended development of its **Didipio project** . This will allow the company to secure financing later, when the financing can be agreed on more favourable terms. Exploration activities at **Benguet Corp’s Kingking** copper -gold project on Mindanao Island have been suspended due to lower metals prices. Kingking, which has an estimated resource of 353 Mt grading 0.35% copper and 0.439 g/t gold. _Thomson Reuters, January 12_<sup>_th_</sup> _2009._

**Russia: Russian Copper Co (RCC)** reduced output from its **Kyshtym** refinery by 33% and from its **Novogorod** refinery by 10% in 2008 due to lower co

pper prices, a devaluation of the Rouble, and a shortage of copper scrap. RCC increased mine production to mitigate the scrap supply shortfall, sending blister grade copper to Kyshtym and sending all scrap copper to Novogorod, which only processes scrap. The Kyshtym complex is made up of two plants, one with capacity of 40 ktpy that it suspended in late 2008 and one with an 80 ktpy capacity which remains in operation. The complex treats 70% copper derived from ore and 30% from scrap. The Novogorod refinery has capacity to produce 60 ktpy of cathode. RCC also announced that it has suspended development of a fourth refinery division, in spite of all necessary equipment having been delivered. Its third division, **Uralgidromed** , 

has a capacity of 5 ktpy cathode, but the company did not report its operational status. _Thomson Reuters, January 26_<sup>_th_</sup> _2009._

**Zambia:** The launch of Zambia’s **Chambishi** copper smelter has been delayed. Operations were due to start in December 2008, but are now expected to begin in January 2009. The **Mopani** copper smelter has refused to accept the first copper concentrate shipment from **Equinox Mineral’s Lumwana** copper claiming that the material did not meet contract specifications. Mopani is contracted to take 48 kt of copper-in-concentrate, or 28% of the 170 kt expected to be produced at Lumwana in 2009. The mine started production in December 2008. Equinox says that three other offtakers have accepted the concentrate, but **Glencore** , which owns 73% of the smelter, has declined to comment. _Reuters, January 14_<sup>_th_</sup> _2009._ 

**Vedanta Resources’ Konkola Copper Mines** produced 25 kt of cathode during the fourth quarter of calendar 2008, down from 35 kt in the year earlier period, due to the ramp down of the high cost Nkana smelter. All feed will now be sent to the new Nchanga smelter where recoveries will be higher and operating costs lower. Vedanta has also announced that it will purchase concentrate from **First Quantum’s Frontier** mine in the Democratic Republic of Congo as part of a cost reduction program. The company is also in talks with the **Chibuluma** and **Kansanshi** mines in Zambia to secure concentrate and ore feed for its plants. _Vedanta Resources press release, January 28_<sup>_th_</sup> _& Thomson Reuters, January 6_<sup>_
